<reason>This was a tight, high-quality exchange with real progression on both sides. B built the more inventive case (addition rather than subtraction, warehouse-not-museum realism, scope instability) and landed the debate's sharpest single hit by catching A's test drift from "would he be remembered without the crime?" to "was the statue raised to celebrate the crime?", plus the damaging exploitation of A's "even the tarp is an improvement" and "half the job" concessions. But A held the ground the motion actually occupies. A set a burden — explain why the honor must continue — that B explicitly declined to defend on the merits and then had to meet with the counterintuitive claim that "honor is conferred by framing, not bronze." A's closing rebuttal to that ("twelve feet of bronze on the highest plinth IS the framing; everything else is caption; the position acquits him louder than any placard convicts him") was the cleanest, most decision-ready line in the debate. A also largely defused B's strongest practical route by showing a contextualized site can be cheap (flatbed, signage, fenced lot like Memento Park) and by reversing the funding objection onto B's newly commissioned counter-monument; B's donor-constituency reply was clever but did not undo the point that B's plan leaves the honor standing indefinitely. A's final weighing — "our worst case ends the honor and delays the lesson; their best case delivers the lesson and never ends the honor" — gave the judge the cleanest comparative rule. Both sides answered pressure questions directly with proper labels; A pays a small execution cost for a clipped rebuttal. Narrow but real edge to A.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Two candidates. B's catch that A's scope test mutated between speeches ([A2.6] vs [A4.4]) was the sharpest damage inflicted all debate. But the decisive exchange was A's closing inversion of B's central claim: B argued honor lives in framing and consensus, not bronze; A answered that scale and position ARE the framing, so a caption cannot prosecute a man standing on the city's highest plinth. That neutralized B's whole reason for leaving the statue in the place of civic honor.</best_rebuttal>
